headline: Coupang swings to a loss as incident costs squeeze margins
summary_short: Coupang's Q1 2026 net revenue rose 7.5% y/y to $8,504M, but the company swung to a net loss of $266M (EPS -$0.15) as the November 2025 customer-data incident drove roughly $1.2B in compensation vouchers, cost-of-sales inflation, and a collapse in operating margin to -2.8%.
summary_long: Total net revenue rose 7.5% y/y to $8,504M, but Coupang swung to an operating loss of $242M and net loss of $266M (EPS -$0.15) versus a $107M profit a year ago. The November 2025 data-incident customer-compensation program (roughly $1.2B in vouchers, redeemed mostly in Q1) pushed cost of sales to 73.0% of revenue from 70.7%, while higher fulfillment, technology, and marketing costs lifted OG&A to 29.9% of revenue. Operating cash flow fell 48% y/y to $184M on the lower net income. Coupang repurchased $391M of Class A stock and drew $750M on its revolving credit facility; cash fell modestly to $6,301M q/q while equity fell to $3,930M. No forward guidance was given in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Growth reflects a 3% rise in net revenues per Product Commerce Active Customer and a 2% increase in active customers, partly offset by the data-incident impact and unfavorable FX.
Cost of sales rose to 73.0% of revenue from 70.7%, driven by data-incident customer compensation, supply-chain costs, and lower-margin growth in Developing Offerings.
OG&A rose on higher fulfillment, technology, and marketing costs to support growth, compounding the cost-of-sales increase tied to the data incident.
Operating income swung from a $154M profit to a $242M loss while revenue grew 7.5% — margin compression is arithmetic leverage running in reverse.
The net loss reflects the operating loss plus a negative effective tax rate (-4.3% vs 47.2% a year ago) from unrelieved losses in certain loss-making jurisdictions.
Net margin fell because net income swung negative while revenue still grew — the operating and tax drags outpaced top-line growth.
EPS swings to a loss in step with the net-income decline; the weighted-average basic share count changed little y/y (1,825M vs 1,806M).
Diluted EPS equals basic this quarter because the net loss makes potentially dilutive equity awards anti-dilutive, so no dilution is applied (25M shares excluded).
The year-over-year change was driven by a $380 million decrease in net income, partly offset by working-capital timing in inventory and other assets.
The small q/q decline nets higher capex, $750M drawn under the revolving credit facility, and a $391M share repurchase against operating inflows.
This is a 10-Q with no CEO/CFO commentary; the dominant narrative is the November 2025 data incident, whose roughly $1.2 billion voucher program suppressed growth and margins broadly this quarter.
